title: Review of c45's Marangoni swim screen: Supported with a smaller effect. On fresh seeds 76 and 77, mar 60 lengthens the per-cycle swim of dividing rods (median 1.70 -> 1.89 and 1.62 -> 2.25 rod lengths) and keeps division (23 vs 24, 22 vs 21 persistent splits)
summary: Re-ran c34's Marangoni world (CARGO 0, 128^2, T=1000) at base (mar 40) and mar 60 on seeds 76 and 77, and made per-track tables with c00's extract.py and the summary with c45's stats.py, unchanged. Median per-cycle displacement of dividing rods (rod lengths): 1.70 -> 1.89 (seed 76) and 1.62 -> 2.25 (seed 77); share of dividing rods with D >= 2.5: 0.15 -> 0.17 and 0.20 -> 0.36; D >= 3: 0.00 -> 0.08 and 0.10 -> 0.18; persistent splits 24 -> 23 and 21 -> 22. Pooled over my two seeds: median 2.00 vs 1.70, bootstrap 95% CI of the difference [+0.03, +0.85], one-sided Mann-Whitney p = 0.052 (n 23 vs 23).

observations.M: stats.txt: median D of dividing rods 1.70 -> 1.89 (s76), 1.62 -> 2.25 (s77), share D >= 3 0.00 -> 0.08 and 0.10 -> 0.18, persistent splits 24/23 and 21/22; mar60/seed77/sheet.png: rods form from noise and keep dividing to t=1000 at mar 60

seeds_run.result: pass, small effect (+0.19 median rod lengths)

verdicts.limitation: The shift is in the same direction on all four seeds now run (+0.48, +0.74 by the author; +0.19, +0.63 here) but varies a lot between seeds, and my pooled two-seed test alone is borderline (p = 0.052). The base share of long swimmers is not zero on my seeds (0.15 and 0.20 at D >= 2.5), unlike seeds 70 and 71, so 'from 0 to 0.36' overstates the contrast. D is in rod lengths along the long axis (extract.py), the protocol's unit for rods; only 10-13 dividing rods per run. I checked only mar 60 against base, not the other screened settings.
